# Economy

Topics on the industries, institutions, and economic development of South Korea, from post-war reconstruction to its position as a high-income, technology-leading economy.

<!-- BEGIN GENERATED: category-index — maintained by build-structure; do not edit by hand -->
- [Chaebol (Korean Conglomerates)](chaebol.md) — The family-controlled conglomerates that dominate the South Korean economy and drove its rapid industrialization.
- [Semiconductors and Technology Leadership](semiconductors.md) — South Korea's global leadership in memory chips through Samsung and SK Hynix, and its strategic and geopolitical significance.
- [Technology Sector and ICT Innovation](technology-sector.md) — South Korea's ICT, display, AI, telecommunications, gaming, and mobility industries beyond semiconductors; the innovation ecosystem behind a high-income economy.
- [Automotive Industry](automotive-industry.md) — The Hyundai–Kia–Genesis manufacturing complex, its rise to the world's third-largest automaker, and its EV, hydrogen, and battery strategy.
- [Banking and Finance Sector](banking-and-finance.md) — The state-engineered directed-credit banking system, the 1997 Asian Financial Crisis and IMF bailout, post-crisis restructuring, and the fintech and internet-only-bank revolution.
- [Energy and Resources Policy](energy-resources-policy.md) — A resource-poor economy's strategy across nuclear power, coal, LNG, and renewables; the state energy enterprises and the nuclear phase-out and its reversal.
- [Labor and Employment Policy in South Korea](labor-employment-policy.md) — The evolution of labor relations from authoritarian control through the 1987 Great Workers' Struggle to today's regular/non-regular dual labor market.
- [Petrochemicals and Heavy Chemical Industry](petrochemicals-heavy-chemicals.md) — The naphtha-cracking and heavy chemical sector built around Ulsan, Yeosu, and Daesan; a top-tier global exporter of plastics and fibers now facing Chinese overcapacity and a shift toward specialty and green chemistry.
- [Shipbuilding Industry in South Korea](shipbuilding-industry.md) — The chaebol-integrated "Big Three" yards (HD Hyundai, Hanwha Ocean, Samsung Heavy Industries) that lead the world in LNG carriers and high-value vessels, their developmental-state origins, cyclical downturns, and green-shipping transition.
- [Tourism Industry in South Korea](tourism-industry.md) — International and domestic tourism and the Hallyu-driven visitor boom; Jeju, heritage, food, and MICE tourism; the industry's economic weight; and the COVID-19 shock and recovery.
- [Naver](naver.md) — South Korea's largest internet company and search portal; an integrated platform ecosystem spanning search, webtoons, payments, cloud, and AI, with Japan's LINE messenger among its holdings.
- [Construction Industry and Real Estate Development](construction-industry.md) — The third major industrial pillar — chaebol-led megaprojects and Middle East contracts, the apartment-and-jeonse housing system, the speculative real-estate cycle, and the labor, safety, and project-finance challenges of the 2020s.
- [Telecommunications Industry](telecommunications-industry.md) — The SK Telecom, KT, and LG U+ operator market and Samsung network equipment behind South Korea's mobile and broadband leadership, from 1980s liberalization through the world-first 5G launch to the 6G roadmap.
- [Pharmaceutical and Biotech Industry](pharmaceutical-biotech-industry.md) — The life-sciences pivot from generics to biosimilars and CDMO leadership, led by Samsung Biologics, Celltrion, and SK Bioscience, and Korea's rise as a global clinical-trial and biomanufacturing hub.
- [Kakao](kakao.md) — South Korea's mobile-first platform conglomerate, built on the dominant KakaoTalk messenger and expanded into payments, internet banking, mobility, gaming, and entertainment; the other half of the Naver–Kakao internet duopoly.
- [K-beauty and Cosmetics Industry](kbeauty-cosmetics-industry.md) — The cosmetics and skincare export sector and soft-power engine led by Amorepacific and LG Household & Health Care; multi-step skincare, the cushion compact, the indie-brand and TikTok booms, and the THAAD-era China shock.
- [Healthcare System in South Korea](healthcare-system.md) — The universal single-payer National Health Insurance system, its 1977–2000 development and 99% coverage, the private-provider delivery model, healthcare financing and cost control, the pharmaceutical and aesthetic-surgery sectors, and challenges from population aging, mental health, and the 2024 medical-school-expansion doctors' walkout.
- [LG Group and LG Electronics](lg-group.md) — One of the Big Four chaebol, from its 1947 "Lucky" and GoldStar origins to its present portfolio spanning home appliances, OLED displays, EV batteries (LG Energy Solution), chemicals, and telecommunications, and its 2021 exit from the smartphone business.
- [Korean Tech Startups and Venture Capital Ecosystem](tech-startups-venture-capital.md) — The startup and venture-capital economy that grew alongside the chaebol from the 2010s — unicorns such as Coupang, Toss, Krafton, and Baemin, the VC and government-funding landscape, the Seoul–Pangyo clusters, and the 2022–2023 funding correction.
- [Korean Ginseng Industry and Herbal Medicine](ginseng-industry.md) — Korea's distinctive ginseng (*Panax ginseng*) sector and traditional herbal-medicine (*hanbang*) tradition — from the *Dongui Bogam* and the Joseon state monopoly to Geumsan cultivation, red-ginseng processing, KGC's Cheong Kwan Jang brand, ginsenoside research, and the licensed Oriental-medicine system.
